title: Pierce Brosnan, Fiona Shaw, Cara Delevingne and Gabrielle Union Throw a Lavish Christmas Party in New Burberry Campaign

body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Burberry is throwing a Christmas party fit for Hollywood.

	The British luxury house has enlisted Pierce Brosnan, Fiona Shaw, Cara Delevingne, Gabrielle Union and Dwyane Wade for its 2026 holiday campaign, a star-studded celebration of the brand’s 170th anniversary directed by filmmaker Harmony Korine.

	Titled “Wrapped in Burberry: Celebrating 170 Years,” the short film takes place at Longleat House, a historic English estate in Wiltshire, where Brosnan and Shaw play hosts to an extravagant holiday gathering. The guest list also includes Brosnan’s son Dylan, “Bridgerton” star Nico Parker, “Pachinko” actress Kim Min-ha and Chinese actor Wu Lei, with a cameo from Emma Thynn, Marchioness of Bath.




	

	





	

	





	

	



	The festivities unfold through a series of quintessentially British holiday activities — countryside walks, party games, gift exchanges and golf buggy races — before culminating in a glamorous disco beneath an oversized mirror ball. Set to Sylvester and Patrick Cowley’s 1982 dance track “Do You Wanna Funk?,” the film sees the former James Bond star showing off his moves on the dance floor, while Shaw eventually retreats to the sofa after a long night of celebrations.

	“We wanted to celebrate 170 years of Burberry with a proper party,” said Daniel Lee, the brand’s chief creative officer. “Family, friends, great gifts and everyone dressed up.”

	The campaign marks another fashion collaboration for Korine, the filmmaker behind “Spring Breakers” and “Gummo.” Earlier this week, Gucci unveiled its holiday campaign helmed by Korine, starring Mariah Carey.


	Alongside the film, Burberry is introducing a holiday collection centered on cashmere, including new iterations of its signature Kensington trench coat in ivory, black, navy, camel and bouquet pink. The collection also includes cashmere capes with shearling collars, embroidered sweaters and the brand’s Scottish-made House Check scarves, available in more than 40 colorways.

	Other holiday offerings include velvet vanity cases, check bouclé handbags, children’s versions of the brand’s signature outerwear and even a line of accessories for dogs, including check sweaters and bandanas.

title: Versant CEO: MS NOW Not Suffering From ‘News Fatigue’ Like Fox News
description:
If Fox News’ viewers are growing weary of the headlines, MS NOW‘s are not.

	Viewers of the Versant Media-backed cable outlet appear to be growing
body:
If Fox News’ viewers are growing weary of the headlines, MS NOW‘s are not.

	Viewers of the Versant Media-backed cable outlet appear to be growing more interested, not less, in the current news cycle, according to remarks made by Mark Lazarus, the company’s CEO, to investors Tuesday.  Lazarus was responding to a question about the state of interest in news following comments made Monday by Fox Corp. CEO Lachlan Murdoch, who said Fox News’ audience had “viewer fatigue,” which had resulted in a ratings downturn in both the third quarter and October.
	

	“We are not seeing any of that viewer fatigue,” Lazarus said, suggesting that recent growth in MS NOW’s ratings may be fueled by audiences who are leaving other networks. “I think some of the viewership is leaving other places and trying us, and spending some more time with us because I think they’re seeing the value in what we’re providing,” he said.

	Neither CEO said as much, but the executives stand on opposite sides of the red-vs.-blue divide. Viewers at Fox News, which caters to a conservative crowd, have likely been put off by growing poll projections that call for Republicans to lose seats in both the U.S. House and Senate on Election Day. Meanwhile, MS NOW’s audiences, which tilt left, are no doubt encouraged.

	Indeed, Lazarus called MS NOW’s coming Election Day coverage would be a stand-out event. “Today is the Super Bowl for the news organization,” the executive said. “We believe we will continue to grow audiences for MS NOW.”

	“I mean, we’re not seeing, currently not seeing any fatigue with our audiences. Our audiences are active and vibrant and growing for MS NOW, and for that matter, with CNBC,” Lazarus added.
	

	To be sure, the audience for Fox News Channel continues to dwarf that of its competitors.  Fox News won an average of 2.06 million total viewers in primetime in the third quarter, compared with 930,000 viewers at MS NOW. Among viewers between 25 and 54 — the demographic most coveted by advertisers — Fox News captured an average of 183,000 in primetime, compared with 84,000 at MS NOW.

	But Fox News’ numbers are eroding, while MS NOW’s are growing. The primetime averages for Fox News in the third quarter fell 17% among overall viewers and nearly 25% in the advertiser demo. MS NOW’s primetime averages were up 16% in total viewers and up 27.3% among viewers between 25 and 54.

	On Monday, Murdoch suggested a spate of big stories, including flooding in parts of the U.S. and the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, had lured bigger audiences in the past year and raised the bar in terms of year over year audience comparisons. But he didn’t feel Fox News was losing its audience. “Those viewers are not going to any other news channel,” Murdoch said during the analyst call. Instead, he suggested, “they are just fatigued and watching slightly less television.” Executives at Fox News Media, he said, have seen the dynamic before and have a “playbook” and know how to navigate the trend.

	If Lazarus seemed to be tweaking his contemporary, well, Murdoch kind of started it. During the Fox call on Monday, he indicated he did not think much of Fox News’ rivals. “You can’t really call them peers, but our cable news competitors,” he said.

schema.headline: Versant CEO: MS NOW Not Suffering From ‘News Fatigue’ Like Fox News

title: Tristan Thompson Boards Jason Zada’s Bitcoin Creator Movie ‘Satoshi’ as Producer (EXCLUSIVE)
description: A new feature film titled “Satoshi,” about Bitcoin’s pseudonymous creator Satoshi Nakamoto, is set to be directed by Jason Zada (“The Forest, “Terr
body:
A new feature film titled “Satoshi,” about Bitcoin’s pseudonymous creator Satoshi Nakamoto, is set to be directed by Jason Zada (“The Forest, “Terrarium”) with backing from former NBA champion and tech investor Tristan Thompson. The plan is to start shooting in Saudi Arabia and Los Angeles in spring 2027.

	Tristan Thompson — who is known in the tabloids for sharing two children with Khloé Kardashian — will produce “Satoshi” alongside Enderby Entertainment principals Rick Dugdale and Dan Petrie Jr.
	

	“Satoshi” is among the first projects under a multi-picture deal between Enderby Entertainment and Saudi Arabia’s Yellow Camel Studios production company. The plan is to shoot the film at JAX Film Studios, a state-of-the-art production complex in the Saudi capital city of Riyadh.

	The creator of Bitcoin, whose identity and invention remain secret, is also the subject of the Doug Liman-directed film “Bitcoin” (aka “Killing Satoshi”) which has a cast including Casey Affleck, Pete Davidson, Gal Gadot and Isla Fisher. “Bitcoin,” which is currently in post, has sparked controversy for using AI to create the movie’s sets and lighting, having been reportedly filmed in just 20 days inside a “gray box” studio in London.

	Also on board “Satoshi” as producers are BDE Ventures founder and Bitcoin and cryptocurrencies pioneer Brian D. Evans, as well as actors Aaron Arnold (“Splitting Image”) and Austin Arnold (“Splitting Image,” “Altcoin Daily”), according to a statement from Enderby Entertainment.

	“Satoshi” will examine the origins of Bitcoin, which was created in 2008 in the wake of the global financial crisis as a way to circumvent traditional financial institutions.
	

	Zada and Nate Atkins (“Take This Lollipop”) partnered on the shooting script, based on an original screenplay by Cam Cannon (“Zero Contact”). Zada, who is the founder of the AI-native studio Secret Level, is currently in production on the AI hybrid horror feature “Terrarium.”

	However, while AI will be used as a tool in making “Satoshi,” AI is “not the main focus of how the film will be made,” according to a rep for the film. “This is a traditional film production, including on-location filming, etc.,” the rep stated.

	The “Satoshi” logline reads: “A troubled FBI agent partners with a charismatic defense attorney under federal pressure to unmask Bitcoin’s elusive creator, Satoshi Nakamoto — plunging into a high-stakes crypto thriller of government overreach, personal demons, and a mystery that still defies the world.”

	“Bitcoin wasn’t born in a boardroom. It was released as open-source code by someone who chose to disappear,” Dugdale said in a statement. referring to the ongoing effort to unmask the mysterious Satoshi Nakamoto, author of the bitcoin white paper which laid the theoretical foundations for modern digital currencies.

	“We’re not interested in a sanitized version of that story,” he added. “We’re bringing in people who understand the code, the culture and why it mattered from the beginning.”

	“Jason has been pushing the edges of how films get made, and with the support of the Saudi kingdom we have the room to do this properly,” the “Satoshi” producer continued.

	Commented Thompson: “We are entering a new financial era where money moves at the speed of the internet, value flows seamlessly across borders and entirely new systems of ownership and exchange are emerging. Satoshi sparked a movement that is fundamentally reshaping how the world thinks about wealth, freedom and financial power.”

	Evans underlined that “for years, the traditional media has misunderstood Bitcoin and the people who built it,” and pointed out that this film “isn’t about unmasking Satoshi. It’s about getting the narrative and story right for the world to finally see.”

	Enderby Entertainment was founded in 2006 and has previously produced “Blackway,” starring Anthony Hopkins, Julia Stiles and Ray Liotta, which premiered at Venice in 2015; Ben Kingsley-starrer “An Ordinary Man”; “Night Hunter Henry” with Henry Cavill, Ben Kingsley and Alexandra Daddario; and the three-film anthology based on Swedish writer Hakan Nesser’s “Intrigo” trilogy of novels.
	

	Zada is repped by UTA and Dante DeSario at Collage.

schema.headline: Tristan Thompson Boards Jason Zada’s Bitcoin Creator Movie ‘Satoshi’ as Producer (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Behind Election Night Scenes, Fox News Launches New Multimedia Era
description: On Fox News, the stars of Election Night are usually Bret Baier, Martha MacCallum and Bill Hemmer. This year, some of the most important players wi
body:
On Fox News, the stars of Election Night are usually Bret Baier, Martha MacCallum and Bill Hemmer. This year, some of the most important players will rarely be seen on camera.

	New control rooms are debuting Tuesday evening at the Fox Corp.-backed outlet that allow producers to move content more easily across its many platforms, whether they be TV, streaming, digital or social. The idea, says Doug Rohrbeck, Fox News’ executive vice president, Washington news and politics, is to allow for quicker distribution of the content and information being collected from reporters and correspondents, rather than having a report earmarked for one particular opportunity, like a segment on a TV program or a video for social media.
	

	“You really want to share reporting and resources across the company,” says Rohrbeck, during a recent interview, in order to “reach more people without duplicating the entire operation.”

	Fox News is, like its TV-news brethren, operating at a time when audiences have spread out across a panoply of different viewing windows. Some might watch live TV. Others might stream a show on demand via a streaming outlet like Fox Nation, or jump from one clip to another of similar subjects on the subscription outlet Fox One. Some followers may keep up with the news by keeping track of Fox News correspondents like Trey Yingst as they post videos on social media outlets.

	“We don’t want to try to silo the content,” says Rohrbeck. “We want to have it all there and each platform can sort of curate what they think works best for their users. But it’s really sharing all of the reporting, all of the data.”
	

	On Election Night, Fox News will have several different operations going on at once.

	Fox News Channel and Fox Business Network will simulcast the company’s signature Election Night coverage, led by Baier and MacCallum, with Trace Gallagher handling overnight hours. Meanwhile, Fox Nation and Fox News Digital will stream “Ruthless Live!” from a Washington D.C. bar with co-hosts Josh Holmes, Michael Duncan, John Ashbrook, and Shashank Tripathi offering perspective on what shapes various state races. Fox News users will for the first time be able to ask an AI-powered chatbot questions about specific races and voting trends and get answers drawn from the outlet’s reporting.

	The recalibrated operations nod to the fact that different users are, as “Ruthless” co host Josh Holmes says, “experiencing news and information differently.”

	Fox News has in recent years been paying more attention to people who may not watch its TV lineup in day-and-date fashion. The company has spread its resources into books, audio and digital, and launched streaming products built around weather and lifestyle programming, among other niches.

	The wider aperture comes as linear TV companies grapple with splintering audiences. On Monday, Fox CEO Lachlan Murdoch acknowledged that Fox News is working its way through some “viewer fatigue” with news that caused a downturn in third quarter and October ratings. Competitors have noticed the trend in recent weeks, which surfaces ahead of midterm elections that polls have suggested are likely to be favorable for Democrats, and not the Republicans who are Fox News’ strongest audience.

	Murdoch appeared sanguine about the dynamic, noting that Fox News executives have a “playbook” and know how to navigate the trend. They did it in the lead-up to the 2006 midterms, when President George W. Bush was an incumbent Republican whose approval ratings were in decline. Even so, news aficionados have never had so many competing options offering high-quality video and information.

	The news audience may be spread out, but many different parts of Fox News are working to corral them. “We take all the different divisions of our company into this,” says Bill Hemmer. “You will see me on TV, but we’ve got a politics team, a graphics team. We’ve got an augmented reality team.” They’re doing what any modern news organization has to do in the streaming era — placing equal importance on many different media types.

schema.headline: Behind Election Night Scenes, Fox News Launches New Multimedia Era

title: U.K. Celebrity Loses Injunction Bid to Prevent Sexual Misconduct Allegations From Being Published, but Will Remain Anonymous Pending Appeal
description: An anonymous U.K. celebrity has lost his injunction bid to prevent two news organizations from publishing sexual misconduct allegations against him
body:
An anonymous U.K. celebrity has lost his injunction bid to prevent two news organizations from publishing sexual misconduct allegations against him and therefore revealing his identity.

	Earlier this month, it was reported that an anonymous celebrity had applied for a permanent injunction at London’s High Court to try to stop ITN and The Guardian from publishing a story containing allegations that he abused his power to engage in “inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women,” according to BBC News. The celebrity denies the allegations.
	

	Judge Mr. Justice Nicklin rejected the injunction request on Tuesday, as reported by BBC News, but the celebrity will remain anonymous for the time being to allow him a chance to appeal the judgement.

	“The claimant’s claim for an injunction was dismissed,” Nicklin said in his ruling. However, he added: “The court did not determine whether the allegations, or any of them, were true, and the dismissal of the claim does not amount to approval of any publication the defendants may decide to make.”

	The lawyer for the celebrity told the court earlier that should he lose the injunction and the stories publish, it was “highly likely” he would attempt to commit suicide. According to his lawyer, he has already attempted to do so twice before. 

	ITN and The Guardian’s lawyer, on the other hand, argued that publishing the allegations and the man’s identity is in the public’s best interest. He said that the news organizations had spoken to over 100 people in their investigation and that many of the women “have been traumatized by the claimant’s alleged conduct and have suffered mental health crises and mental illness as a result,” according to BBC News.
	

	The unusual case has sparked much conversation in the U.K. amid widespread speculation about the celebrity’s identity, as well as concern for potential ramifications on press freedom. on Monday, Variety spoke with defamation lawyer Paul Tweed about the likelihood that the celebrity’s request would be approved due to his mental health.

	“The court don’t grant that very lightly — they’ll be very thorough in their examination of whether there is a genuine risk of suicide, or whether that is being used just an excuse, basically,” Tweed said, though he acknowledged that a “threat to life” is one of very few “main grounds that are remaining” for an injunction such as this in today’s world.

schema.headline: U.K. Celebrity Loses Injunction Bid to Prevent Sexual Misconduct Allegations From Being Published, but Will Remain Anonymous Pending Appeal

title: ‘Blue Eye Samurai’ Sets Season 2 Release Date at Netflix
description:
Netflix has announced the Season 2 premiere date for “Blue Eye Samurai.” 

	The second season of the popular adult animated series will debut on th
body:
Netflix has announced the Season 2 premiere date for “Blue Eye Samurai.” 

	The second season of the popular adult animated series will debut on the streamer on Jan. 19, 2027. That is more than three years since the first season aired in Nov. 2023. 

	The official logline for Season 2 states, “In Season 2, Mizu’s (Maya Erskine) bloody quest continues in London, where she faces new friends, old foes, and her own demons. In Japan, Akemi (Brenda Song) and Taigen (Darren Barnet) navigate Edo Castle under a dangerous new Shogun, while Ringo (Masi Oka) searches for new purpose.
	

	Along with Erskine, Song, Barnet, and Oka, the cast of the series’ second season includes Jonathan Pryce, Joel Kim Booster, Sherry Cola, and more. Season 1 cast members included Kenneth Branagh, George Takei, Randall Park, Stephanie Hsu, and Ming-Na Wen among several others. 

	Michael Green and Amber Noizumi are the creators, writers, and executive producers on “Blue Eye Samurai.” Erwin Stoff is also an executive producer. Jane Wu serves as supervising director and producer. Blue Spirit serves as the animation studio. 

	It was announced back in August that “Blue Eye Samurai” has already been renewed for a third season, which will also be the show’s last. The final season is slated to debut in 2028. 

	The first season of “Blue Eye Samurai” ultimately won four Creative Arts Emmy Awards back in 2024, including the award for Outstanding Animated Program, beating out shows like “Scavengers Reign,” “The Simpsons,” “X-Men ‘97,” and “Bob’s Burgers.”

schema.headline: ‘Blue Eye Samurai’ Sets Season 2 Release Date at Netflix

title: Creators Pounce on Midterm Elections, Hoping to Win New Viewers and More Dollars
description: Scott MacFarlane has traded in the desk once sat behind at CBS News on Election Night for something more direct — livestreamed midterms coverage fo
body:
Scott MacFarlane has traded in the desk once sat behind at CBS News on Election Night for something more direct — livestreamed midterms coverage for the progressive outlet MeidasTouch.

	He won’t have someone manipulating a Magic Wall or Big Board. He won’t be introduced by swelling orchestral music. And he won’t be competing with colleagues for precious minutes of airtime. MacFarlane will be ready to talk to followers via streaming channels starting at 7 p.m. Tuesday.
	

	At a traditional TV outlet, says MacFarlane, his contribution would have been curated by producers. This year, he says, “the voice we get to use is my voice. I am going unscripted, without a teleprompter, just telling people point blank what’s happening.”

	Dozens of independent journalists will do the same.

	Coverage of returns on Election Night has long been dominated by the nation’s big TV-news outlets. This year, however, so-called “creators” — indie journalists and non-traditional experts — want their own piece of the audience.

	In addition to the MeidasTouch stream, which will feature MacFarlane along with former MSNBC host Katie Phang, former NBC News political guru Chuck Todd will hold forth with colleague Chris Cillizza in a live stream they call “The Projection.” It will appear across YouTube, X, Substack, Decision Desk HQ’s Votes portal and Noosphere, one of many new subscription platforms that offers access to the work of expert journalists. Piers Morgan, whose Uncensored company won millions in funding late last year, is traveling from London to host several nights of coverage in the nation’s capital. Jim Acosta and Katie Couric, two popular former mainstream TV anchors, will team up to host a live stream from the University of Virginia, and have booked guests including Rahm Emanuel, Pete Buttigieg and Tara Setmayer. Don Lemon, the former CNN anchor, will greet guests such as Joy Reid and Hunter Biden while presiding over a show in a New York City bar.  Even staid CSPAN is getting in on the craze, and plans to simulcast hours of coverage from progressive outlet The Young Turks and conservative commentator Patrick Bet-David.
	

	Despite some of the hosts’ mainstream roots, many of them think they can bring viewers something the legacy outlets cannot.

	“This will be Murdoch-Ellison-free coverage,” says Acosta of the show he and Couric plan to put on, making a direct nod to the ownership of Fox News by the Murdoch family and the control over CBS News and CNN now enjoyed by the Ellison family, which controls the newly formed Skydance. “Katie and I are free to let it rip.”

	The ability to speak frankly and with little corporate oversight isn’t the main reason pundits and independents are gathering. Many of these people see a big opportunity to generate subscriptions, advertising and revenue — and to draw bigger audiences to their various outlets in an era when the economics of media are decidedly in flux.

	“I think this is a precursor to what we are going to see in two years, with more audiences coming to platforms like ours, along with more top-tier guests, and more newsmakers,” says Rashida Jones, who was named CEO of Morgan’s company in May after a stint running MSNBC. Advertisers were eager to sponsor Morgan’s shows from Washington, D.C., she says. A good Election Night showing by Morgan, she says, can only generate new audiences and business.

	Will there be enough of both to help all these companies thrive? About 58% of U.S. adults see social media as a key means of staying current with the news cycle, according to a recent Pew Research Center survey. Approximately 13% indicated social media was the most important way to get news. When Pew issued a similar survey in 2022, 43% of Americans said social media was an important way they got news, and 5% said it was the most important.

	“The crowd’s going to keep on growing,” says Jones. “This is the turning of the corner of that audience coming to digital-first platforms.”

	The independents aren’t the only ones who see a growing opportunity. Mainstream media is also seeding the ground. Fox Nation, the Fox News streaming outlet, will run a three-hour live special led by the team behind the popular Ruthless podcast. Josh Holmes, one of the co-hosts, says he will likely not drink alcohol even though the event will take place in front of a crowd in a Washington D.C. bar.

	“We will try to keep a sense of humor about topics that people often get sort of negative about, and then we always provide what we think is an under-the-hood look at serious topics,” says Holmes. The team doesn’t see the livestream as competing with Fox News coverage led by Bret Baier, Martha MacCallum and Bill Hemmer, says Holmes. “Wwe are supplementing that, trying to give some perspective.” Several “Ruthless” members have jobs as strategic political advisers and can offer unique insights.
	

	NBC News this year is launching its first vertical-video program, led by anchor and correspondent Gadi Schwartz. He will be on the ground in Texas and will talk with various NBC News journalists based in different parts of the country. The program will “really look at a more conversational approach to how the night is unfolding,” says Catherine Kim, NBC News’ executive vice president of editorial, and will play out not only on the company’s social media feeds, but also Schwartz’ own.

	Independents who once had a strong foothold in legacy media may have the best chance of surviving. Couric and Acosta booked their own guests and are taking a strong hand in designing the look and feel of their Election Night program.

	“We both worked for a long time with legacy media, and I think it made the transition to a digital platform much easier for us, because we came in with a built-in audience to a certain extent,” says Couric. “We want to have both of our audiences intersect and come together on Election Night, and it will be hopefully good for both of us.”’

	The duo say they know which elements of news presentation to keep and which to jettison. Delivering important information is in. Doing it in an overly formal way is not.

	“We want to make it unlike what the networks are doing,” says Acosta. “We are not going to be overly stilted and scripted and all of that stuff. This is much more freewheeling.”

	And, potentially, blunt. Couric says she can say things that NBC and CBS would never have allowed her to state when she worked for them on programs like “Today” and the “CBS Evening News.”

	“I think we are liberated,” says Couric. “I don’t think our hands are tied in the way that network anchors are with their corporate overlords breathing down their necks.”

	And since the program will be done on their own terms, Couric and Acosta can also relax — well, at least a little bit. “We are going to be much more casually dressed than I was when I did election coverage for CBS,” says Couric. “There might be an open bar,” says Acosta.

schema.headline: Creators Pounce on Midterm Elections, Hoping to Win New Viewers and More Dollars

title: Olga Kurylenko and Alex Pettyfer to Star in Crime Thriller ‘Breakwater,’ WestEnd Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Olga Kurylenko (“Quantum of Solace,” “Oblivion,” “Black Widow”) and Alex Pettyfer (“Magic Mike,” “The Butler,” “The Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfa
body:
Olga Kurylenko (“Quantum of Solace,” “Oblivion,” “Black Widow”) and Alex Pettyfer (“Magic Mike,” “The Butler,” “The Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfare”) are set to star in crime thriller “Breakwater,” which has been boarded for world sales by WestEnd Films.

	The film, directed by Luc Walpoth (“In Tandem,” “Dead Money”), is set to begin production in April 2027. WestEnd will launch sales at the upcoming American Film Market.
	

	Set in a sun-soaked coastal paradise, “Breakwater” follows two women desperate for a way out. Iris (Kurylenko) is trapped in a toxic marriage, while Daya is a bartender desperate to escape her dead-end hometown.

	A chance encounter brings them together, and they hatch a plan to blackmail Iris’ sadistic husband Avery (Pettyfer) aboard his luxury yacht. But what seems like the perfect escape quickly spirals out of control. Stranded on the high seas, with nowhere to run and no one to trust, Iris and Daya find their carefully laid plan turning into a fight for survival.

	The film is produced by Kurt Wimmer (“The Beekeeper 1 & 2,” “Law Abiding Citizen,” “Point Break”), Jib Polhemus (“The Mechanic,” “Lara Croft: Tomb Raider,” “The Expendables 2”), Hannah Leader (“Mary,” “Freud’s Last Session,” “A Visit to Grandpa’s”) and Tad Daggerhart (“Black Lotus,” “Coyotes”), who also penned the script (“Expend4bles,” “Black Lotus”). James Ireland (“Echo Boomers”) executive produces for Dark Dreams Entertainment.

	“Breakwater” reunites WestEnd with Polhemus following their collaborations on action thriller “Scorpion,” also starring Pettyfer, alongside Clive Owen (currently in post-production), and “Zealot,” starring Kodi Smit-McPhee and Djimon Hounsou.
	

	Production in Malta will be overseen by Malta Film Service, led by partners Jean Pierre Magro and Vadim Fortunin. With credits including “Not Without Hope,” “Hounds of War” and “Blood on the Crown,” the company will manage on-the-ground line production, local crew integration, and rebate structuring across the shoot.

	Walpoth said: “’Breakwater’ is a Mediterranean neo-noir thriller about lust, greed, betrayal and the desire to escape. Set against a gorgeous coastal backdrop, the film contrasts sun-drenched beauty with the darker tensions beneath the surface. Visually, I want to create a world that feels both sensual and unsettling, building from simmering suspense into a propulsive, high-stakes thriller as plans unravel and loyalties shift on the open sea.”

	Maya Amsellem, managing director of WestEnd, said: “’Breakwater’ is a gripping thriller with a fantastic cast in Olga and Alex and a hugely experienced creative team behind it. Luc has a distinctive cinematic vision for the film, blending the atmosphere of classic noir with the pace and intensity of a contemporary thriller. We’re delighted to be teaming up again with Jib Polhemus on such an exciting project, and look forward to introducing the film to buyers at AFM.”

	WestEnd’s wider AFM slate includes new supernatural horror “Sketchbook,” starring Woody Norman and Billie Piper (shooting early 2027); Tim Blake Nelson’s “The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd,” starring Amanda Seyfried and Scoot McNairy (screening at AFM); “A Visit to Grandpa’s,” starring Academy Award winners Anthony Hopkins and Catherine Zeta-Jones (in post-production); “Margot & Rudi,” a romantic drama directed by Anthony Fabian, starring Naomi Watts (in pre-production); action-thriller “Scorpion,” starring Pettyfer and Owen (in post-production); high-concept thriller “Ignition,” starring Maisie Williams; and “Unspeakable,” a horror from Corinna Faith, starring Eliza Scanlen and Essie Davis (in post-production).

schema.headline: Olga Kurylenko and Alex Pettyfer to Star in Crime Thriller ‘Breakwater,’ WestEnd Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)

title: WWE, Disney Team for ‘Avengers: Doomsday’-Themed Worlds Collide, John Cena Classic
description:
WWE and The Walt Disney Company are teaming for an “Avengers”-themed collaboration. 

	Expanding on WWE’s existing relationship with ESPN, WWE will
body:
WWE and The Walt Disney Company are teaming for an “Avengers”-themed collaboration. 

	Expanding on WWE’s existing relationship with ESPN, WWE will take over the ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex at the Walt Disney World Resort for two days this December. The takeover will kick off with the John Cena Classic on Dec. 14, followed by the premium live event “Worlds Collide” on Dec. 15, which will be “Avengers: Doomsday”-themed ahead of the film’s release on Dec. 18. 
	

	As previously announced, the John Cena Classic will feature stars from across WWE, with Cody Rhodes already set to participate. Members of Club WWE, WWE’s fan membership program, will then get to vote in real time for their favorite superstar of the night, who will be awarded the John Cena Classic Championship. The event will stream live on Netflix as a special edition of “Monday Night Raw.”

	“Worlds Collide” will feature WWE stars as well as talent from lucha libre promotion AAA, which WWE acquired in 2025. 

	WWE and Fanatics will also brinbg WWE World for both days of the event, giving fans access to exclusive merchandise and photo and autograph opportunities with WWE Superstars. WWE will also produce and sell “Avengers: Doomsday” co-branded products, including title belts, at WWE World, WWEShop.com and across select Disney retail stores.

	Two-day combo tickets will go on sale starting Nov. 13 at 10 am ET via Ticketmaster. General presale for combo tickets will begin Nov. 12 at 10am ET. Additional event and fan experience details will be announced in the coming weeks.

title: Josh O’Connor Describes Bond Rumors as ‘Incredibly Bizarre Pinch Me Moment’: ‘To Be Considered Is Extraordinary’
description: Josh O’Connor is the latest James Bond contender to address speculation surrounding the coveted role, calling the prospect of succeeding Daniel Cra
body:
Josh O’Connor is the latest James Bond contender to address speculation surrounding the coveted role, calling the prospect of succeeding Daniel Craig an “incredibly bizarre pinch me moment.”

	The “Challengers” and “The Crown” actor, who is rumored to be one of the finalists in the search for the next 007, told the BBC that he was “very honored” to have his name in contention.

	“It’s an incredibly bizarre pinch me moment…even being uttered in that same sentence and being considered for something like that,” O’Connor said while attending the opening of the Everyman Theatre’s new education and community center in his hometown of Cheltenham, England.
	

	“To be considered in that same sort of bracket is extraordinary,” he added, before declining to elaborate on his potential involvement. “But I am afraid, there is nothing to say beyond that.”

	O’Connor is reportedly among a handful of actors undergoing final screen tests for the role, alongside “Slow Horses” actor Jack Lowden and “Masters of the Air” actor Callum Turner.

	Lowden also recently addressed the speculation, telling British GQ that the attention was “all very flattering” but that he wasn’t “going to add to the noise.” 

	The next Bond film, the 26th installment in the long-running spy franchise, will mark the first since Amazon MGM Studios assumed creative control of the property from longtime custodians Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson in 2025.

	“Dune” filmmaker Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the currently untitled film, with a screenplay from “Peaky Blinders” creator Steven Knight. Amy Pascal and David Heyman will produce, while veteran casting director Nina Gold has been tapped to lead the search for the next Bond.
	

	The casting process has generated months of speculation, with Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Jacob Elordi, Paul Mescal, Harris Dickinson and James Norton among the actors previously linked to the role.

            The anonymous celebrity in the United Kingdom who told a judge he may die by suicide if outed will be identified ... a judge in the country has ruled.
      
    
            According to The Sun, the celebrity cannot be named just yet while a potential appeal is considered. The allegations involve claims he abused his fame and status over several years to pursue inappropriate sexual relationships with numerous girls and young women ... allegations he denies.
      
    
            As we reported ... lawyers for the unknown celeb asked the judge to rule that the celebrity's name not be revealed by two major news outlets because of the possibility he may harm himself.
      
    
            His attorneys insisted this was not an admission of guilt ... but instead a concern about being put through a "trial by media."
      

            ITN and The Guardian's lawyers argued the suicide risk could be reduced with treatment and that the allegations are too important to keep out of the public eye.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The judge, Matthew Nicklin, acknowledged the seriousness of the case ... calling it "difficult and important" while stressing the court must weigh the evidence fairly.
      
    
            The judge previously warned the general public against trying to identify the celebrity ... warning they could end up behind bars themselves if they continued to do so.
      
    
            If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat 988lifeline.org.

            The passengers on the private jet that crashed in Florida have been identified ... they were a family of four from Texas ... and they were traveling with their nanny and two friends ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Onboard the Learjet 60 that crashed Sunday were 44-year-old Austin tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson, plus his wife Helen, their two kids, and two close friends ... sources close to the family tell TMZ.
      
    
            The Robinsons had their nanny with them ... and the two pilots also died.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            We broke the story ... the captain was 55-year-old Jeff Gregory.
      
    
            His co-pilot was 20-year-old Nathalia Gadelha. She earned her pilot's license when she was just 17 years old, doing so before she even graduated high school.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            The private jet was flying from Austin to the Bahamas when it took a nosedive and crashed in Florida. Video shows the jet plummeting from the sky, nose-first, as it explodes on a busy street.
      
    
            The NTSB held a news conference Monday, confirming ice began forming on the jet in the middle of moderate turbulence. The crew asked to increase altitude from 35,000 feet to 37,000 feet shortly before an emergency was declared.

NYC Marathon Runner

            Tragedy struck Sunday's New York City marathon after a young woman running the race collapsed and died a mere 2 miles from the finish line.
      
    
            The New York Times reports Rachel Apa was running in her first marathon with her Parkinson’s Champions team to honor her late grandfather, who passed away from the disease in 2022. 
      
    
            As she was closing in on the finish line, Apa suddenly collapsed, and a hospital social worker watching the marathon rushed over to give CPR along with Apa's fiancée, the NYT said.
      

            But nothing could be done to save Apa, a former field hockey player for Bucknell University, who had trained for months for the 26-plus mile run and was in “perfect health, perfect shape,” according to her father, Steve Apa.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
            The Times says Steve was tracking his daughter’s movements using the marathon app, and Apa's mom, Michelle, shot a video of her when she arrived at the 14th mile mark -- and she was "beaming."
      
    
            Apa sent 2 text messages to her dad saying "Ow" at the 18th and 19th miles -- and her dad texted back at the 23rd mile saying "Final stretch." He never received a response.
      
    
            A rep for the NYC Medical Examiner's Office tells TMZ ... On Monday, doctors performed an autopsy on APA, but her cause and manner of death are pending further study.
      
    
            Apa was 24.
      
    
            RIP

'Dukes of Hazzard' John Schneider
                          I Owe My Ex-Wife Million$ ...

            'Dukes of Hazzard' star John Schneider is changing course in his divorce battle with his ex-wife, Elvira Schneider ... he's now admitting he owes her millions ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            In court docs, obtained by TMZ, the actor says he was confused because there were two divorces filed … one in California and one in Louisiana. He says he didn't initially think the support order from California was valid but says he now understands he owes around $3.7 million in back spousal support to his ex.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The actor says he does not seek forgiveness … but doesn't want her to take half of his Social Security checks until the debt is paid off.
      

            John says he is not "financially capable of satisfying the accumulated arrearages, and an order diverting one-half of his Social Security benefits would substantially affect the resources available" for him to pay his monthly bills.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As TMZ first reported, Elvira claimed she was owed millions in back support, alleging he owed more than $2.3 million in back support and around $1 million in interest.
      
    
            The exes split in 2014 after 21 years of marriage. In 2019, John was ordered to pay $25k a month in support, and Elvira has been attempting to collect that money for years.
      
    
            John previously disputed the amount owed but has apparently waved the white flag over the amount owed.
